title: The Match I Was Definitely Winning
scene: You play table tennis with a friend and start unusually well. Early success makes you more ambitious, the simple game disappears, and you end up explaining how well things might have gone if you had continued playing normally.
sceneJa: 友人との卓球で最初の3ポイントを取り、前回より上達した気になる。しかし難しいショットを狙い始めて崩れ、最後には『最初の40秒だけうまい』という妙な戦術だけが残る。

あまり苦労せずに

前回一緒にプレーしたときに
だから今回は〜のように感じました
大きな進歩に
私はボールを打ち返し始めました
少し強気に

chunks.ja: さらに何本かのショットまで試しました
普段なら避けるような
すると1本ミスし
続けてもう1本ミスして
急にスコアが
あまり面白くなくなりました

chunks.en: By the middle of the game,

一方、友人は

chunks.ja: 見たところほとんど何も変えておらず
ただ続けていただけでした
ボールを返すことを

高度な戦術を

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: I told myself / to keep things simple / which lasted for about two points / before I attempted another ambitious shot
I told / myself to keep / things simple which / lasted for about two points
I told myself to / keep things / simple which lasted / for about two points
questions.explanation: The first version separates the self-instruction, the useful phrase ‘keep things simple’, and the contrast showing how quickly the plan failed.

questions.question: What does ‘keep things simple’ mean here?
options: Avoid unnecessary complexity and play a straightforward game
questions.explanation: ‘Keep things simple’ means avoiding unnecessary complexity and sticking to a straightforward approach.

questions.question: What is the joke in the final sentence?
options: The speaker invented a real advanced technique
The speaker reframes a brief good start as if it were a strategy
The friend only played for forty seconds
questions.explanation: The speaker dryly describes a short period of good play as a ‘highly advanced strategy’, exposing the gap between early confidence and the final result.

speak: Start confident but casual. Let the confidence rise slightly in the third sentence, then flatten as the mistakes arrive. Read ‘much less interesting’ and ‘generally considered part of the game’ very straight. Keep the final sentence calm and precise rather than punchy.
review: Flow: strong start → growing confidence → unnecessary ambition → loss of simple play → post-match explanation → dry reframing. Useful chunks: ‘keep things simple’, ‘not so much A as B’, and ‘point out that ...’. The humour comes from treating forty seconds of good table tennis as though it were a sophisticated strategy.
